title: terraform-gpu-pools-multi-scaler-abstraction-and-healthchecks-for-private
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that models GPU node pools for Redwood Private with an abstraction that supports multiple scalers (ASG and Karpenter) and provides robust health checks and upgrade hooks for GPU drivers. Module should be opinionated about lifecycle patterns, safe defaults for mixed spot/ondemand pools, and expose configuration for autoscaling policies, canary pools, and driver upgrade sequencing.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module variable interface documented (variables.tf) and validated with terraform validate
Module can provision GPU pools using ASG and Karpenter via flags without additional forking
Health-check hooks exist that wait for NVIDIA driver + device plugin readiness before marking nodes ready
Driver upgrade path implemented as optional lifecycle hook with safe rollback semantics
E2E test (terratest) asserts autoscaling behavior for scale up/down and spot fallback
Migration guide written: from legacy-gpu-pool -> new multi-scaler module
PR merged and deployed to staging private cluster; metrics show no regressions in node readiness or pod disruption

implementation_notes: We use composition: module contains two child modules (asg_pool and karpenter_profile) and selects which to instantiate based on variable 'scaler'
Spot fallback: configure mixed instances for ASG and node-template for Karpenter with 'prefer_spot' boolean and separate fallback pools for ondemand
Driver bootstrap: use a DaemonSet image 'rw-gpu-driver-init' with a node-local lockfile and a null_resource remote-exec for initial node taint removal
Healthchecks rely on two signals: k8s node Ready + GPU device plugin reported metrics (nvidia.com/gpu count > 0), implement exponential backoff probes
Module exposes outputs: node_pool_id, node_pool_labels, instance_types, scaler_type, drift_detection_id
Avoid provider-specific long-lived resources in top-level module; keep state compact and add optional remote state export
design_decisions: Decision: prefer a single module with internal composition vs multiple separate modules to reduce user cognitive load
Decision: default to mixed spot pools with an explicit 'ondemand_fallback' pool instead of inline fallback to reduce noisy preemption impact
Decision: implement driver upgrades as opt-in (variable 'enable_driver_upgrades') to avoid surprise upgrades during routine infra changes
Decision: lifecycle create_before_destroy for critical ASG resources to preserve capacity during nodegroup changes
risks: Spot preemption can cause service disruption if autoscaling policies are aggressive - mitigated by conservative default target utilization and ondemand fallback
Driver install failures could leave nodes unschedulable - mitigated by canary pool + staged rollout and automated rollback script
Karpenter autoscaling semantics differ across cloud providers; abstraction may leak provider assumptions - document provider-specific knobs
Terraform state drift if external processes modify nodegroups outside module - add drift_detection_id and recommend single source of truth
testing_plan: Unit: terraform validate + fmt on module and child modules
Integration: terratest that provisions into a short-lived Private VPC test account, asserts node readiness and GPU availability
Chaos: simulated spot preemption to verify ondemand fallback works and that workloads recover
Upgrade test: run driver upgrade flow on canary pool and assert no more than 10% PDB impact
Staging rollout: deploy module to staging private cluster and run smoke tests for 48 hours
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module behind feature flag in Private platform. 2) Provision a small canary pool (1-2 nodes) with 'enable_driver_upgrades=true' and run the upgrade flow. 3) If canary stable for 6 hours, gradually migrate low-criticality stacks to new pools in 10% increments. 4) Monitor node readiness, kube-scheduler pending pods, and GPU metrics; rollback if >5% increase in P50 scheduling latency.
